paper.title_en: A Five-Dimensional Geometric Formulation of Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
paper.abstract_en: We apply a geometric formulation of Newtonian dynamics to inviscid compressible geophysical flow, with gravity and the effects of rotating or moving coordinates incorporated in the metric tensor. This construction relies on the introduction of an auxiliary fifth coordinate, which allows mass and momentum transport, internal energy, and pressure work to be combined into a single mass--momentum tensor. The covariant divergence of this tensor leads to the continuity equation for mass density, the three momentum equations, and the thermodynamic equation, with the system closed by an equation of state. A time-independent metric also yields conservation of total energy. We recover familiar forms of the equations and illustrate the construction in rotating spherical and terrain-following coordinates. The thin-shell and spherical-geopotential approximations, with constant effective gravity, simplify the metric while retaining vertical gravity and the traditional Coriolis terms. Emphasis is placed on the connection between the geometric structure of the formulation and the equations commonly used in atmospheric dynamics.
